title: Study of Cell Migration in Microfabricated Channels
protocol: Mix PDMS oil and curing agent at a weight ratio of 10:1 in a plastic cup.
Mix both compounds thoroughly.
Cast the mix over the mold bearing microchannels with a total height between 0.5-1 cm.
Remove air bubbles in a vacuum jar bell for 1 hour.
Harden PDMS in the mold by placing it in an oven at 65 °C for 2 hours.
Once the PDMS is at room temperature, cut a large piece around the structure with a surgical blade and peel it off from the mold.
Drill holes where cells will be injected (typically 2 mm).
Resize the PDMS with a surgical blade to fit the size of glass-bottom dishes in which migration will be assessed.
Remove residual dust from the dish using lens cleaning paper before proceeding.
Clean the resized PDMS chip containing the channels by sticking and peeling adhesive tape on the structure sides.
Sonicate the PDMS pieces for 30 seconds in 70% ethanol to remove dusts and small PDMS particles.
Dry the PDMS quickly by blowing clean air.
Activate the PDMS (structures upwards) and culture dishes by air plasma treatment for 30 seconds at 300 mTorr.
Place both activated surfaces in contact to permanently stick the PDMS to the substrate.
Use metallic forceps to press slightly on top of the PDMS if necessary, to ensure contact between the polymer and the glass of the dish.
Incubate the chip in the oven at 65 °C for 1 hour to strengthen the binding.
Activate the entire structure by air plasma at 300 mTorr for 1 minute.
Fill rapidly the entry holes of the chip with fibronectin at 10 μg/ml in water.
Check that the liquid spreads throughout the entire structure under regular light or using a bright field microscope.
Incubate the chip at room temperature for 1 hour to allow adsorption of the fibronectin to the walls of the channels.
Wash the structures 3 times with PBS to remove nonbound substrate.
Remove PBS from the plate.
Fill the microsystem with cell medium.
Incubate for 1 hr to saturate the channels with the medium.
Remove floating DCs.
Recover semi-adherent cells by flushing with culture medium.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Stain nuclei with Hoechst 33342 at 200 ng/ml in complete medium for 30 min if nucleus imaging is required.
Wash stained cells twice by centrifugation to remove excess dye.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min.
Discard the medium and resuspend the pellet.
Dilute the cell suspension to reach a concentration of 20 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Remove excess medium from the plate using a micropipette.
Empty entry holes in the PDMS structure with a micropipette.
Fill each entry hole with 5 μl of cell solution containing 1 x 10^5 cells.
Incubate the microchip for 30 min at 37 °C in the incubator.
Add 2 ml of complete medium to the experiment dish.
Clean the external bottom surface of the dishes with lens cleaning tissue before placing the plates under the microscope.
Use 10X magnification and wide field illumination in a CO2 and temperature-equipped video-microscope for analysis.
Facilitate cell tracking by using Hoechst staining and UV light.
Analyze migration using confocal microscopy to get higher resolution of cellular structures during migration.
Choose a time frequency according to the expected cell speed for time-lapse microscopy at 10X.
